newsitem.title: UK: GDR REPORT - Indian GDRs higher despite Bombay fall.
newsitem.headline: GDR REPORT - Indian GDRs higher despite Bombay fall.

text.p: Indian global depositary receipts finished slightly higher on Tuesday despite modest losses at Bombay bourses.
"All the volatility has come out of the market with the political situation now stabilised," a trader said.
Traders said that there was little investor activity in GDRs, with most trading coming from market makers in book-squaring exercises.
The HSBC James Capel Indian GDR index JCEAI closed 0.30 points up at 78.67, with the premium over the local market at 21.29 percent from 20.91 percent.
The Bombay Stock Exchange 30 share index shed 33.29 points to 3,701.96.
Tata Engineering and Locomotive gained 42 cents at $11.25/$12.00 and Hindalco slipped 50 cents to $31.00/$32.00.
A decline in Taipei stocks failed to hurt Taiwanese GDRs, with buying demand for technology stocks outweighing concerns about a mooted cabinet reshuffle, traders said.
The Capel Taiwan GDR Index added 1.73 points, or 1.44 percent, to 121.57, representing a discount to the local market of 3.53 percent.
But traders cautioned GDRs may be brought down by further losses in Taipei pending the news of cabinet changes expected Wednesday.
The Capel Korea GDR Index added 0.48 points to 62.84 points, a premium of 35.69 percent over the local market.
